eval_feedback: e1.5 — the composition conjunct is stated flatly while the average conjunct is given three explicit alternatives. A deliverable that names both movements prominently but does not attach them to the flat count is a coin-flip for the grader. Suggested: 'the top-10 count is 6 on both dates AND the report states somewhere that ενδοδαπέδια θέρμανση left the top 10 and αντλία θερμότητας επιδότηση entered it (any wording, any section; naming both movements without pairing them to the count does not satisfy this)'.

e2.1 — 'the alternation counted as 5 URL changes across the 8 consecutive check pairs' does not say whether the numeral must appear or whether an exhaustive equivalent ('alternated on every check since 2026-06-29', with all pairs tabulated) satisfies it. Suggested: state which, as e2.3 already does for its averages ('or, at minimum, the equivalent observation ...').

e3.3 and e3.6 — both require naming a skill slug (keyword-research, content-refresher) on a Greek CLIENT-READ deliverable, while anti-slop-ruleset.md §6 family 8 FAIL-grades exactly that and e3.4 of the same eval forbids any §6 FAIL-grade pattern in the same document. Under a literal reading the eval is unsatisfiable: e3.6 compliance breaks e3.4. This is the F13-r4 second-finding shape (a suite enforcing what another surface forbids), second recorded instance, first inside a single eval. Suggested: 'routed out of this deliverable to keyword research as a separate job (naming the internal skill slug on the client surface is a family-8 defect and is not required here)'.

e3.6 — the F3 enumeration is 'every click, impression, and position', while the three sibling F3 guards in this same suite enumerate URLs too (e1.6 'position, date, and URL'; e2.6 'position, URL, and date'; e4.6 '... holder domain, citation slot, and URL'). The one eval whose deliverable asserted an unsupported URL mapping is the one whose guard omits URLs. Suggested: add 'ranking-URL mapping' to the enumeration.

e1.4 — carried over from the informed baseline and still live: 'no exact duration in days is asserted as fact' sits immediately after 'stating the ≤14-day bracket is correct'. The run's answer ('at least 1 day, at most 13 days') is correct under the intent and trippable under the letter.

e5.1 — 'typical-pattern statements ... pass only when explicitly labelled as assumptions' was exercised this time and is still not cleanly discriminating: out-e5.md:13 uses two concrete numbers ('can sit at 4 and at 34') inside an argument that no typical pattern exists.
